name: Elixir of Agony
summary: In Tarren Mill, Elixir of Agony is being prepared for a cruel trial. Apothecary Lydon, acting for the Royal Apothecary Society, means to test a deadly poison disguised as stolen dwarven ale on human prisoners.

sections.title: A Deadly Vintage
sections.body: Apothecary Lydon gathers foul ingredients across the Hillsbrad Foothills and steals dwarven ale from Dun Garok. The Royal Apothecary Society has charged him with making a deadly brew called Elixir of Agony. Once mixed, the poison waits inside a keg that appears to hold ordinary mountain stout.

sections.title: Unfortunate Guests
sections.body: Deathguards in Tarren Mill recently seized local human farmers, suspecting that a military strategist from Stormwind was hiding among them. Word came that the strategist had died in the Plaguelands. High Executor Darthalia then judged the surviving farmers useless for military intelligence and handed them to Lydon for his chemical trials.

sections.title: Testing the Brew
sections.body: Lydon’s tainted keg is carried upstairs to the holding room and set on a dusty rug before the thirsty captives. Unaware of the danger, the farmers hurry to drink. The poison takes hold within moments, and they collapse dead, showing how lethal the brew is.

faq.q: Why were the human farmers captured in the first place?
faq.answer: Deathguards captured the farmers because they suspected a military strategist from the Kingdom of Stormwind was hiding among them. After the strategist died in the Plaguelands, High Executor Darthalia no longer considered the captives useful for intelligence.
Apothecary Lydon belongs to the Forsaken’s Royal Apothecary Society and works in Tarren Mill. He develops and tests lethal blights and poisons meant to eradicate the living, often on captured locals.

faq.q: Where did the ale inside the keg come from?
faq.answer: The ale came from the dwarves of Dun Garok, a stout mountain stronghold in the southern Hillsbrad Foothills. Lydon tainted the stolen keg with his reagents so its deadly poison would seem to be ordinary dwarven brew.

faq.q: What happens when you deliver the tainted keg?
faq.answer: Lydon asks you to place the tainted keg on the rug in the prisoners’ room for his experiment.

faq.q: Who authorized using the prisoners as test subjects?
aliases: who let lydon test on farmers
faq.answer: High Executor Darthalia, commander of the Forsaken forces in Tarren Mill, gave the surviving prisoners to Apothecary Lydon after they no longer had military value.

faq.q: What is the Royal Apothecary Society trying to achieve here?
faq.answer: The Royal Apothecary Society seeks to make a deadly blight that can destroy both the Scourge and the living. Field trials such as Elixir of Agony test new ways to deliver chemicals and measure their effects on human bodies.

angles.text: As Forsaken, you know the Royal Apothecary Society’s poisons are vital to survival. They seek to secure the Hillsbrad Foothills from a human resurgence by any means.
As a human, you see the Forsaken’s cold ruthlessness in the slaughter of helpless Lordaeron farmers, their former kin.
As Horde, you witness the harsher side of Forsaken operations in Tarren Mill, where they test the limits of what others are willing to accept.
